title: 사장님 시범 한 번
oneLiner: 사장님이 반복 업무를 한 번 보여주면 단계를 풀어 쓰고 딱 한 단계만 자동화해 세 번 나란히 검증하는 노코드 대신 시범 도구.
theme: 역전 — one demonstrated routine becomes leverage without turning the owner into an automation engineer.
targetUser: Korean small-shop owners, clinic administrators, academy managers, and service businesses without IT staff.
keyUX: capture demonstration, bind feedback to exact steps, label human judgment and system dependency, choose one safe candidate, run manual and assisted lanes side by side three times, then issue a repair/fallback card.

sourceSignals.note: Small businesses want setup translation, one automated step, and a repair path.

mechanic: record one 90-second routine, point to the painful step, select exactly one automation candidate, and compare three shadow runs.
triggerMoment: the owner repeats the same copy/paste task for the third time today.
buyerShareAudience: owners, local digital-transition consultants, franchise field staff, and accountants.
userActionSentence: “노드는 모르겠고, 제가 하는 걸 한 번 보여드릴게요.”
threeSecondSting: a split view says “90초 시범에서 8단계 발견 · 자동화는 1개만”.
outputArtifact: verified one-step macro card with trigger, inputs, human checkpoint, break signs, and manual fallback.
firstValidationTest: observe ten owners performing a real admin task; compare independent repeatability and recovery after an injected failure.
lovedBySmallGroup: 4/5 — shops with one owner-operator and no IT staff feel every broken automation personally.
smallGroupFit: businesses where the owner is also the process expert can test one task without migrating systems.
spreadTrigger: the owner can hand a one-page “what changed / how to do it manually” card to staff or a consultant.
referencePattern: screen recording + apprenticeship demonstration + shadow-mode macro.
twist: the product refuses multi-workflow “transformation”; one observed step must pass three shadow runs and keep a manual fallback.
firstScreen: one 90-second recording with eight extracted step frames and a hard “choose one” gate.
shareOrPlayLoop: demonstrate → point → select one → shadow-run three times → approve or discard → share repair card.
planBrief: User problem: tool builders understand nodes; owners understand embodied routines. Inflow: consultant referral or repeated admin pain. Business: per-workflow clinic or partner kit. Core loop: record → step frames → point → classify → one candidate → three shadow runs → repair card. First screen: real task filmstrip. Rules: one automation only; every human judgment remains explicit; stop on mismatch. QA: hidden clipboard, login prompt, changing spreadsheet column, staff variation, no network, undo, readable Korean. Risk: recordings contain sensitive data; prototype uses redacted mocks.
developmentStartPrompt: Build a Korean workflow clinic with a 90-second mocked demonstration, editable step filmstrip, exact-step comments, human-versus-machine labels, a one-candidate gate, three side-by-side shadow runs, injected mismatch, stop/undo, and a repair/manual-fallback card. Do not expose an automation node canvas.
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive Korean small-business tool called “사장님 시범 한 번” for shop, clinic, academy, and service owners who understand their routine but cannot configure Make or n8n. The observed pull is explicit: owners want someone to turn messy work into a checklist, automate one piece, and leave a way to fix it. Open on a 90-second recorded task—copying Kakao inquiries into a booking sheet—with eight visual step frames and the hard limit “자동화는 1개만.” Let the owner point at the painful frame, edit the step wording, mark human judgment, choose one safe candidate, and compare manual versus assisted results across three shadow runs. Inject a changed spreadsheet column on run three; the flow must stop, explain the mismatch, undo safely, and produce a repair/manual-fallback card for staff. Required sections: recorder, step filmstrip, exact-step feedback, judgment flags, one-candidate gate, three shadow runs, mismatch review, stop/undo, repair card, and handoff. Emotional pressure: repetitive admin without dependence on an unrepairable black box. Design direction: use the operator-dense profile with charcoal and slate surfaces, one amber action accent, compact 36–40px rows, crisp manual/assisted state labels, square-to-8px controls, and no node canvas, chatbot layout, or AI gradient.
